Let
\[
\rho_x=\frac{1-\omega_x}{\omega_x}.
\]
Then
\[
\rho_x=\begin{cases}
1/3,& \omega_x=3/4,\\
3,& \omega_x=1/4,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\mathbb E\log\rho_0=(1-2\theta)\log 3.
\]

The key point is that direction depends on \(\mathbb E\log\rho_0\), while speed and first-passage means depend on moments of \(\rho_0\) or \(\rho_0^{-1}\), not on the averaged drift.

For a nearest-neighbor RWRE on \(\mathbb Z\), the standard one-dimensional product criterion comes from solving the harmonic equation for hitting probabilities. For \(a<x<b\),
\[
P_\omega^x(T_b<T_a)
=
\frac{\sum_{k=a}^{x-1}\prod_{j=a+1}^{k}\rho_j}
{\sum_{k=a}^{b-1}\prod_{j=a+1}^{k}\rho_j}.
\]
Letting \(a\to-\infty\), \(b\to+\infty\), the behavior is governed by products
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n \rho_j
=
\exp\left(\sum_{j=1}^n\log\rho_j\right).
\]
By the law of large numbers,
\[
\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n\log\rho_j\to \mathbb E\log\rho_0=(1-2\theta)\log 3.
\]

Hence:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
\theta<1/2: & X_n\to-\infty,\\
\theta=1/2: & \text{recurrent},\\
\theta>1/2: & X_n\to+\infty.
\end{cases}}
\]

Now compute the moment criteria. We have
\[
\mathbb E\rho_0=\theta\cdot\frac13+(1-\theta)\cdot3
=\frac{9-8\theta}{3},
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\rho_0^{-1}
=\theta\cdot3+(1-\theta)\cdot\frac13
=\frac{1+8\theta}{3}.
\]

For crossing from \(0\) to \(1\), the quenched expected time satisfies
\[
E_\omega^0T_1
=
1+2\sum_{k\le0}\prod_{j=k}^{0}\rho_j.
\]
Averaging over the environment gives
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_1
=
1+2\sum_{m\ge1}(\mathbb E\rho_0)^m,
\]
so this is finite exactly when \(\mathbb E\rho_0<1\), i.e.
\[
\frac{9-8\theta}{3}<1
\iff
\theta>\frac34.
\]
When finite,
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_1
=
1+2\frac{\mathbb E\rho_0}{1-\mathbb E\rho_0}
=
\frac{1+\mathbb E\rho_0}{1-\mathbb E\rho_0}
=
\frac{6-4\theta}{4\theta-3}.
\]

Similarly,
\[
E_\omega^0T_{-1}
=
1+2\sum_{k\ge0}\prod_{j=0}^{k}\rho_j^{-1},
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_{-1}
=
1+2\sum_{m\ge1}(\mathbb E\rho_0^{-1})^m.
\]
This is finite exactly when
\[
\mathbb E\rho_0^{-1}<1
\iff
\frac{1+8\theta}{3}<1
\iff
\theta<\frac14.
\]
When finite,
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_{-1}
=
\frac{1+\mathbb E\rho_0^{-1}}{1-\mathbb E\rho_0^{-1}}
=
\frac{2+4\theta}{1-4\theta}.
\]

Thus the speed is ballistic to the right if \(\theta>3/4\), ballistic to the left if \(\theta<1/4\), and zero otherwise. Explicitly,
\[
\boxed{
v(\theta)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{4\theta-1}{2+4\theta}, & 0<\theta<\frac14,\\[6pt]
0, & \frac14\le \theta\le \frac34,\\[6pt]
\dfrac{4\theta-3}{6-4\theta}, & \frac34<\theta<1.
\end{cases}}
\]

The walk is transient but has zero limiting speed exactly for
\[
\boxed{\theta\in(1/4,1/2)\cup(1/2,3/4]}.
\]
At \(\theta=1/2\) it is recurrent with zero speed.

Finally, the three transition parameters are
\[
\boxed{(\theta_-,\theta_{\rm dir},\theta_+)=\left(\frac14,\frac12,\frac34\right)}.
\]
